subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should sandbox image APT resilience be retry-only, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept `--fix-missing` semantics with explicit package-presence verification?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` directly addresses transient fetch failures, while `--fix-missing` can let required packages be held back after retrieval or integrity failures, so the final contract needs owner intent before the linked PR lands.

options.title: Use retry-only APT hardening
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` on update/install commands and remove `--fix-missing`, then require proof that both sandbox images build and contain expected packages.

options.title: Accept `--fix-missing` deliberately
options.body: Keep `--fix-missing` only if maintainers want partial-install semantics and add package-presence verification that fails incomplete images.

options.title: Defer until live repro
options.body: Leave current fail-closed Dockerfiles unchanged until a reproducible network-failure log proves that retry-only hardening is needed.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT hardening
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` on update/install commands and remove `--fix-missing`, then require proof that both sandbox images build and contain expected packages.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the sandbox-common builder and workflow and is the strongest history-backed owner for the final sandbox image contract choice.
